hypothesis: A probability-derived fair margin is useful only if a chronology-estimated margin scale maps pregame win probabilities to realized margins competitively. The audit will test the bridge directly rather than infer quality from winner accuracy.
bridge_rule: For validation season S, estimate sigma_margin as the standard deviation of actual home margin minus market spread using only completed seasons < S. Then fair_margin = sigma_margin * Phi^-1(P_home). No sigma tuning or scale multiplier search.
qualification_rule: A probability bridge may be described as a predictive fair-margin model only if its MAE is not materially worse than market spread with blocked uncertainty. The market-plus-football bridge must additionally improve the raw-market bridge with uncertainty support to justify football-driven movement in the public fair line.
interpretation_guardrail: Failure does not invalidate winner probabilities; it means probability-to-points is a presentation transform rather than a validated margin forecast and must be labeled accordingly.
prohibited_inputs: full-sample sigma estimated using validation outcomes
final_decision: Not qualified as a predictive margin model. Preserve only as an explicitly labeled probability-consistent presentation transform unless a separately pre-registered future experiment demonstrates predictive margin qualification. Do not tune sigma after this result.
